title: Transient signal rescoring experiments — notes and proposed runbook changes
content:
Summary:

We ran a signal rescoring experiment to reduce pager noise from transient, low-signal observability spikes that were contributing to SLO burn alerts and on-call fatigue. This doc captures motivation, experiment design, quantitative results, qualitative observations from oncall shifts, and proposed short/medium-term runbook changes.

Why we did this (background):
- Over the last 3 quarters we've seen repeated bursts of transient metrics (short-lived spikes in downstream RPC latency, ephemeral `kv_cache_miss` blips) that trigger our high-priority SLO burn alerts.
- Pager volume during these bursts spikes by ~2.3x but median incident TTL and impact are often negligible (auto-resolve within 60-120s).
- Traditional static thresholds + rate/aggregate windows are either too slow to catch real incidents or too sensitive to transients.
- Need: reduce noise while preserving detection sensitivity for real degradations and cascading failures.

Problem statement:
- Current alerts treat every threshold breach as equal pulse; duplicates and context are not scored.
- When multiple related metrics spike together (e.g., backend-a latency + cache misses), we don't reliably prioritize which signal matters.
- Oncall spends cycles chasing transient alerts that are non-actionable, increasing cognitive load and slowing response for true incidents.

Hypotheses:
1) Rescoring alerts using temporal context (age since last breach), cross-signal correlation, and duplicate suppression will reduce false positive pager volume by >= 30% without increasing time-to-detect for real incidents by > 20%.
2) Lightweight rescoring that runs in the alerting plane (before paging) will be cheaper and easier to iterate on than full-blown ML models in the pipeline.

Experiment design (high-level):
- Implementation: augment pre-paging pipeline with a rescoring function that calculates an "alert score" in [0,100] using:
  - recency factor: exponential decay for repeats within 5m, 15m, 60m windows
  - correlation boost: +X when related metric families (latency, 5xx, cache_miss) co-occur within 2m
  - duplicate penalty: -Y when source/process hash matches recent alerts
  - severity baseline: base score from SLO importance and current burn rate
- Page threshold set to score >= 60 for this experiment (control: baseline rules without rescoring).
- A/B rollout: 25% of oncall paging routed through rescoring for 3 weeks (Nov 20–Dec 11), remainder baseline.
- Key metrics collected: pager_count_per_day, pagers_per_oncall_shift, median_time_to_ack, percent_incidents_with_actionable_remediation, daily_slo_burn_minutes, silent_auto-resolves (% of incidents that auto-resolved within 2m).

Instrumentation notes:
- Added `rescore_reason` tag to all pre-paged events for traceability (values like RECENT_REPEAT, CORRELATED, DUPLICATE_REDUCED, HIGH_BURN_OVERRIDE).
- Sampled raw event payloads (1%) stored to staging bucket for offline analysis (link in linked_artifacts).

Quantitative results (aggregate across experiment window):
- Pager volume: -38% in treatment group vs control (p < 0.01).
- Pagers_per_shift: median from 7 -> 4 (treatment).
- Median time_to_ack: +9% (from 4.1m -> 4.5m) in treatment; distribution skew increased slightly (95p at 22m -> 26m).
- Daily SLO burn minutes: no statistically significant increase (treatment delta +0.7%, within noise).
- Silent_auto-resolves: treatment decreased from 31% -> 18% (we saw fewer auto-resolves being paged because rescoring suppressed transients).
- Actionable incident ratio (incidents that required remediation by a human): improved from 22% -> 34% in treatment (higher precision).

Qualitative findings (from oncall debriefs):
- Oncall reported higher confidence in pagers; fewer "check-and-close" pages.
- A few real incidents (2 during the window) were initially deprioritized by rescoring rule due to weak correlation signal; both were caught by secondary SLO-based override within 7m.
- Ops suggested an explicit "override by dependency" tag (if a critical downstream service signals a hard failure, boost upstream related alerts to ensure wake-up).
- Rescoring explanations were helpful for triage — the `rescore_reason` made it clear why something did/didn't page.

Edge cases observed:
- Thundering correlated bursts: when many related signals spike simultaneously, rescoring score aggregation sometimes produced mid-scores (45–55) and required tuning of correlation weight; we adjusted correlation boost mid-experiment (X -> X*1.4) which improved detection in later weeks.
- Long tail of infrequent duplicates from CI agents: duplicate penalty had to ignore alerts from ephemeral CI hosts by whitelisting source labels.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: missed fast-moving incidents if rescoring threshold too aggressive. Mitigation: maintain SLO-burn override at high priority (score override) and set a maximum suppression window of 5m after which repeat breaches will escalate.
- Risk: complexity in runbook understanding. Mitigation: add one-line reason strings to pager messages and expand runbook examples.

Proposed runbook changes (short-term):
1) Replace current pre-paging rule for "SLO burn - critical" with rescoring pipeline behind a feature flag. Keep SLO-burn override active for score >= 90 or if burn rate delta > 2x in 1m.
2) Add new section "Rescore reasons" to the oncall runbook with examples and quick triage flows.
3) Whitelist known noisy sources (CI runners, scheduled batch jobs) in the duplicate penalty logic.
4) Add an explicit manual-repage command for oncall (Slack slash command triggers immediate repage if needed).

Proposed runbook changes (medium-term):
- Formalize dependency-based overrides: ingest service dependency graph (partial) so that when a downstream critical service has a hard error, upstream alerts automatically get a correlation boost.
- Retrain rescoring weights quarterly using feedback data (human-labeled incidents: actionable vs non-actionable).

Action items / TODOs:
- [Priya] Draft a short PR to propagate `rescore_reason` into pager text (ETA: 2026-03-08).
- [Ethan] Create JIRA SRE follow-up for dependency graph ingestion (JIRA-SRE-1220).
- [Lina] Whitelist CI host label set and update duplicate penalty list (ETA: 2026-03-05).
- [Marcus] Produce 90-day post-deploy monitoring dashboard (pager volume, SLO burn, override hits) and add to Redwood Console shared board.
- Train oncall rotation (10m session) on how rescoring works + examples; include in next oncall orientation.

Notes to self / loose ideas (brainstorm):
- Consider a lightweight Bayesian update for score combining rather than heuristic weights; cheap to compute if we keep priors simple.
- Look into integrating with tracing to get causality signals (span error rates -> stronger correlation).
- Explore a probation state: if an alert is suppressed twice within X hours but then recurs with new evidence, escalate to higher weight.

Appendix: example rescore_reason values and what they mean:
- RECENT_REPEAT: same metric triggered in the last T window, score reduced by decay.
- CORRELATED: multiple related metrics triggered together, score increased.
- DUPLICATE_REDUCED: identical source/process already paged recently, penalty applied.
- SLO_BURN_OVERRIDE: explicit override when SLO burn exceeds configured threshold.

End of notes.
